abstract: This study conducts a three-year longitudinal analysis (2021–2023) of affective engagement within a hyperpartisan pro-Bolsonaro network of Brazilian Facebook groups and pages. Using LLM-based content classification, time series analysis, and multinomial regression on over 12 million posts, the authors examine how major political events shaped emotional reactions and interaction patterns toward in-group and out-group political actors. Contrary to the assumption that hyperpartisan communities are stable, impermeable echo chambers, the study finds engagement patterns were highly unstable over time, with a marked shift in 2023 around Lula's inauguration and the January coup attempt characterized by declining emotional intensity, increased internal debate, and weakening opposition responses.
key_claims: Hyperpartisan communities do not behave as stable, predictable echo chambers when observed longitudinally; their affective engagement patterns are unstable and event-sensitive.
Affective engagement is jointly structured by which political actor is mentioned and when, rather than by actor identity or temporal context alone.

A major inflection point occurred in 2023, coinciding with Lula's inauguration and the January coup attempt, marked by declining emotional intensity, rising internal debate, and weaker opposition responses.
Engagement dynamics are shaped more by contextual political events than by fixed ideological positions.

Exposure to adversarial content occurs not only through accidental cross-cutting encounters but also through deliberate brigading by political adversaries, making community boundaries contested rather than protected.
methods: Mixed-methods computational approach analyzing 12,156,409 Facebook posts from 53 groups and 4 pages of a pro-Bolsonaro network identified via VeraAI Alerts (Horizon Europe Vera.ai project), collected through CrowdTangle for January 2021–December 2023.

Construction of two post-level behavioral indices: the Emotional Polarization Index (EPI = (love − angry)/(love + angry)) and the Engagement Balance Index (EBI = (shares − comments)/(shares + comments)), both ranging −1 to +1.

Rolling 30-day window volatility detection (days flagged volatile if rolling SD exceeded the 95th percentile), identifying 96 volatile days aggregated into 7 contiguous instability periods (mean 13.7 days), yielding 1,161,126 posts for further analysis.

Fine-tuning of OpenAI's GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) on 2,245 manually coded posts for six political actor categories (multi-label classification), with 80/20 train/validation split; applied to 712,287 text-containing posts.

Two sets of multinomial logistic regression models (one per instability period) predicting tertile-based EPI and EBI categories from five binary actor-presence indicators, controlling for total engagement and total emotional reaction volume.
findings: The EPI showed extreme boundary clustering (94.3% at ±1) and high temporal volatility; the EBI showed 66% boundary clustering; both shifted markedly over time rather than remaining stable.
Of 96 volatile days, 15.6% clustered within 15 days of the January 2023 coup attempt, while three earlier major events showed no volatile days in their windows.

The GPT-4o classifier achieved 67.7% exact-match accuracy and 0.85 overall F1; Bolsonaro-related entities appeared in 43.2% of posts, Lula-related in 28.2%; the low-performing 'Other' category (F1 0.77) was dropped.

Bolsonaro-related content drove strong love-dominated engagement in 2021–2022 (β up to 1.193) that dropped sharply in 2023 (to β = 0.220 by December), with 2023 showing significant rises in comment-dominated (argumentative) engagement.

Lula references generated increased angry responses in early periods (peaking at β = 0.732 around his sentence annulment) that dissipated over time, while love-reaction suppression weakened through 2023 — suggesting incursions by anti-Bolsonaro users.

Armed forces references produced the most extreme temporal variability, tied to discrete events (September 8 military parade, coup attempt); mainstream media showed unexpected positive share-dominated engagement in 2023 rather than consistent suppression.
contributions: Provides the first systematic long-term longitudinal analysis of affective engagement in pro-Bolsonaro Facebook communities, distinguishing in-group versus out-group responses.
Introduces two replicable behavioral indices (EPI and EBI) as proxies for emotional polarization and amplification-versus-discussion dynamics.
Demonstrates a replicable analytical pipeline combining fine-tuned LLM-based political actor classification with longitudinal volatility tracking, validated for Brazilian Portuguese.
Enriches echo-chamber and affective polarization theory by showing hyperpartisan communities can fracture, adapt, and respond to external pressures over prolonged crisis cycles.
Extends the Global South / Brazilian focus of digital polarization research beyond the predominantly US-centered literature.
framing: The paper positions itself within research on destructive/affective polarization, hyperpartisan online communities, and the 'affective affordances' of social media platforms, engaging debates between homophily/echo-chamber accounts and cross-cutting exposure theories. It centers the underexamined Brazilian (Global South) case and the Bolsonaro-Trump analogy, arguing for longitudinal rather than cross-sectional or event-bound study of polarized digital engagement.
